newsitem.title: USA: MicroCell files IPO for Class B non-voting shares.
newsitem.headline: MicroCell files IPO for Class B non-voting shares.

text.p: MicroCell TeleCommunications Inc filed Friday with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to register an initial public offering of Class B non-voting shares.

The Montreal-based company estimated that the offering could raise a total of $100 million. Net proceeds will go toward building, operating and expanding the company's personal communications services network and to additional working capital needs including operating losses, the filing said.

The underwriters are Merrill Lynch & Co and Nesbitt Burns Securities Inc. The company will apply to list the shares on the Nasdaq National Market. It has applied to have them listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the Montreal exchange.
As of July 31, five shareholders owned about 83.7 percent of the outstanding common shares of the company. The common shares are the only class of voting equity shares of Microcell.
Telesystem Ltd. beneficially owned indirectly about 33.4 percent of the common shares and is "therefore able to exert ignificant influence over the company," the filing said.
